claims.explanation: Mocetinostat is a class I HDAC inhibitor whose selectivity is best explained by dependence on class I HDAC activity and an intact, HDAC-repressible epigenetic/tumor-suppressor program: lines with high HDAC1/2/3 expression, wild-type EP300/CREBBP, and intact ARID1A/SMARCA4 chromatin-remodeling complexes are most sensitive, whereas loss of EP300/CREBBP or ARID1A/SMARCA4 and NF2-driven mesenchymal/mesothelioma or KRAS-driven pancreatic lines are relatively resistant. TP53 mutation is nearly universal and not discriminating, but co-occurring PIK3CA mutation and EGFR/ERBB-family alterations mark sensitive epithelial lines, consistent with HDAC-inhibitor-induced growth-factor and immune-antigen pathway dependence.

primary drug target; class I HDAC inhibition reverses repressive chromatin
loss of EP300 in resistant lines (CAL62, LU99, NCIH1339) impairs the acetyltransferase/HAT balance needed for HDAC-inhibitor response
CREBBP loss in resistant CAL62; HAT loss reduces dependence on HDAC-mediated acetylation balance
ARID1A-mutant lines (OVTOKO, SUIT2, NCIH1793) are among least affected, suggesting SWI/SNF loss buffers HDAC-inhibitor sensitivity
SMARCA4-mutant resistant lines (NCIH1703, NCIH1793, EKVX, NCIH1573) indicate chromatin-remodeler loss reduces drug effect
NF2-mutant mesothelioma/thyroid/sarcoma lines (NCIH2052, ISTMES2, S117, YD8, CAL62) are least affected
KRAS-mutant pancreatic and lung lines (PATU8988S/T, SW1990, SUIT2, NCIH1793) cluster among resistant
PIK3CA-mutant epithelial lines (KYSE70, HCC1954, T47D, HGC27, 253J, BFTC909) are enriched among sensitive
EGFR/ERBB-family-altered lines (KYSE70, NCIH1650, NCIH1792, NCIH1573) are enriched among sensitive
ZEB1-driven EMT/stemness confers resistance that mocetinostat reverses, so high ZEB1 marks lines needing the drug but with resistant baseline phenotype
